what: Mirion Technologies makes instruments and software that detect and measure radiation, used in nuclear power plants, hospitals, defence, laboratories and research.
customers: Nuclear plant operators, hospitals and cancer centres, militaries and government agencies, and research labs.
money: Radiation detection and monitoring for power plants, defence and labs
Dosimetry, radiation therapy quality assurance and nuclear medicine
moat: Strong positions in niche, safety-critical markets where reliability and approvals matter more than price.
risks: Debt and a history of losses after its 2021 SPAC listing
A P/E of about 148 on trailing earnings
The share count rose from 181 million in 2022 to 261 million in 2025
opportunities: Revenue grew from $718 million in 2022 to $1.08 billion over the last twelve months
Turned profitable: net income went from a $277 million loss in 2022 to $29 million
Growing demand from nuclear power, including new reactors
watch: Orders from nuclear power and progress in margins.
view: Mirion sits on a theme that has become popular: the return of nuclear power. Revenue has grown from $718 million in 2022 to $1.08 billion over the last twelve months, gross margin has risen to about 47%, and the company has moved from heavy losses to a small profit.

The valuation reflects that enthusiasm. On trailing earnings the P/E is about 148, and even on next year’s estimates it is about 27. The share count has also grown from 181 million to 261 million, diluting existing holders.

What would justify the price is margin expansion: if operating margin keeps rising from its low base, earnings can grow much faster than revenue. Analysts expect EPS to rise about 22% next year. If nuclear projects are delayed, that growth could take longer.
bull: Nuclear power demand drives orders, margins expand and earnings grow quickly.
bear: Nuclear projects are delayed and the high valuation shrinks.
